tourism.attractions_subtitle: Iconic landmarks that define the Zimbabwean experience.

vicfalls.name: Victoria Falls
vicfalls.desc: One of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, the world's largest sheet of falling water
vicfalls.summary: Known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya (The Smoke That Thunders), Victoria Falls is twice the height of Niagara Falls. Experience white-water rafting, bungee jumping, helicopter flights, and the famous Devil's Pool. The falls are at their most spectacular from February to May during peak flow.

greatzim.name: Great Zimbabwe
greatzim.desc: Ancient stone ruins showcasing medieval African civilization and architectural excellence
greatzim.summary: Built between the 11th and 15th centuries, Great Zimbabwe was the capital of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe. The massive stone structures were built without mortar, showcasing sophisticated engineering. The site gives the country its name and remains a powerful symbol of African achievement.

kariba.name: Kariba Dam
kariba.desc: One of the world's largest man-made lakes, perfect for houseboating and fishing
kariba.summary: Lake Kariba stretches over 5,500 square kilometers along the Zambezi River. Famous for world-class tiger fishing, houseboat holidays, and stunning sunsets. The lake is home to abundant wildlife including hippos, crocodiles, and elephants along its shores. Matusadona National Park offers excellent game viewing.

rocks.name: Balancing Rocks
rocks.desc: Iconic natural rock formations that symbolize Zimbabwe's unique geological heritage
rocks.summary: These gravity-defying granite formations appear on Zimbabwe's currency and are found throughout the country, particularly in Matobo National Park. Formed over millions of years through erosion, the rocks create surreal landscapes perfect for photography, rock climbing, and nature walks.

tourism.other_attractions_subtitle: Beyond the iconic landmarks, Zimbabwe offers diverse landscapes and wildlife experiences across the country.

hwange.name: Hwange National Park
hwange.desc: Zimbabwe's largest park, famous for its massive elephant herds and diverse wildlife.
hwange.summary: Covering over 14,000 square kilometers, Hwange is a premier safari destination. It hosts over 100 mammal species and 400 bird species. The park is world-renowned for its elephant population, numbering in the tens of thousands, and offers some of the best game viewing in Africa.

matobo.name: Matobo National Park
matobo.desc: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its balancing rocks and spiritual history.
matobo.summary: Matobo Hills features a unique landscape of granite whaleback dwalas and broken kopjes. It is a significant archaeological site with one of the highest concentrations of San rock art in Southern Africa and is the burial place of Cecil John Rhodes at 'World's View'.

eastern_highlands.name: Eastern Highlands
eastern_highlands.desc: A cool, mountainous region offering lush forests, waterfalls, and misty peaks.
eastern_highlands.summary: Stretching along the border with Mozambique, this region includes the Nyanga, Vumba, and Chimanimani mountains. It offers a stark contrast to the rest of the country with its alpine scenery, trout fishing, and the highest point in Zimbabwe, Mount Nyangani.

mana_pools.name: Mana Pools National Park
mana_pools.desc: A remote UNESCO site famous for its river-fed pools and walking safaris.
mana_pools.summary: Located in the Zambezi Valley, Mana Pools is known for its incredible beauty and the four large pools formed by the river. It offers a unique opportunity for unguided walking safaris among elephants, lions, and African wild dogs in a raw, prehistoric landscape.

nyanga.name: Nyanga National Park
nyanga.desc: The 'Little Scotland' of Africa, home to Zimbabwe's highest peak and deepest falls.
nyanga.summary: Nyanga is a highland paradise featuring Mount Nyangani and Mutarazi Falls (Africa's second highest). Visitors enjoy fly-fishing, golfing, and the adrenaline-pumping skywalk and zipline over the deep Pungwe Gorge.

gonarezhou.name: Gonarezhou National Park
gonarezhou.desc: The 'Place of Elephants,' characterized by the stunning red Chilojo Cliffs.
gonarezhou.summary: As Zimbabwe’s second-largest park and part of the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park, Gonarezhou is famed for its rugged scenery and iconic red sandstone cliffs. It offers a truly wild experience for those looking to get off the beaten track.

success.objective_subtitle: Showcasing the tangible impact of diaspora engagement across various sectors and communities in Zimbabwe.

leather_goods.title: Leather Goods Export Success
leather_goods.story: A group of Zimbabwean diaspora professionals in Germany connected local leather manufacturers with European retailers. The diaspora network provided market intelligence on German consumer preferences, direct introductions to retail buyers, quality assurance guidance, and ongoing product development support.
leather_goods.testimonial: The ZIGD platform connected us with diaspora members who understood both our craftsmanship and European market demands. Within 18 months, we went from local sales to exporting to three European countries.
leather_goods.author: Tendai Moyo

horticulture_breakthrough.title: Organic Horticulture Breakthrough
horticulture_breakthrough.story: A small-scale farming cooperative achieved EU organic certification with support from diaspora agronomists. The project now exports high-value vegetables to European supermarkets, with diaspora members providing technical expertise, certification guidance, and buyer connections.
horticulture_breakthrough.testimonial: We never imagined our small farm could meet European standards. The diaspora experts walked us through every step of organic certification and connected us directly with buyers.
horticulture_breakthrough.author: Grace Ncube

tourism_lodge.title: Tourism Lodge Investment
tourism_lodge.story: Through ZIGD's crowdfunding platform, 280 diaspora investors pooled $500K to develop an eco-lodge near Victoria Falls. The lodge now generates steady returns while providing employment and supporting local communities. Diaspora investors receive quarterly dividends and enjoy preferential booking rates.
tourism_lodge.testimonial: I invested $2,000 from the UK and now I'm part-owner of a beautiful lodge in my homeland. The transparency through NTIR gave me confidence, and the returns have exceeded expectations.
tourism_lodge.author: Simba Chikwanha

stone_sculpture.title: Stone Sculpture Export Network
stone_sculpture.story: Zimbabwean sculptors gained access to North American art markets through diaspora gallery owners and art dealers. The network provides market insights, handles logistics, and promotes Zimbabwean art at international exhibitions. Sales have tripled in two years.
stone_sculpture.testimonial: Our sculptures are now displayed in galleries across three continents. The diaspora network understood both our artistic vision and international market dynamics.
stone_sculpture.author: Patrick Mavros

tech_startup.title: Tech Startup Diaspora Funding
tech_startup.story: A Harare-based fintech startup raised $750K from diaspora investors through ZIGD's investment platform. The company developed a mobile payment solution for rural areas, now serving 500K+ users. Diaspora investors provided both capital and technical mentorship.
tech_startup.testimonial: Diaspora funding came with more than money—we gained advisors who understood Silicon Valley standards and African market realities. Their guidance was invaluable.
tech_startup.author: Tafadzwa Chidavaenzi

honey_export.title: Honey Export Cooperative
honey_export.story: Rural beekeepers formed a cooperative to export organic honey to Europe. Diaspora food scientists helped achieve EU certification, while diaspora business professionals secured contracts with specialty food retailers. The cooperative now supports 120 families.
honey_export.testimonial: From selling honey by the roadside to exporting to European supermarkets—the diaspora network made this transformation possible through technical support and market connections.
honey_export.author: Rudo Makoni

heritage_tourism.title: Heritage Tourism Package Success
heritage_tourism.story: A tourism operator developed specialized diaspora homecoming packages through ZIGD's platform. The packages combine family visits with cultural tourism, attracting over 1,200 diaspora tourists annually. The business employs local guides, drivers, and hospitality staff.
heritage_tourism.testimonial: We created experiences that help diaspora reconnect with their roots while supporting local communities. ZIGD's platform gave us visibility to our target market.
heritage_tourism.author: Chipo Mutasa

macadamia_nut.title: Macadamia Nut Processing Plant
macadamia_nut.story: Diaspora crowdfunding enabled construction of Zimbabwe's first macadamia processing plant. The facility processes nuts from 200+ small-scale farmers, adding value before export. Government procurement contracts provide stable demand while export markets drive growth.
macadamia_nut.testimonial: We raised $1.2M from diaspora investors who believed in value-addition. Now we're creating jobs, supporting farmers, and exporting premium products to Asia and Europe.
macadamia_nut.author: Ngoni Sibanda
